_comment_howto: Suggested thesis topics, internships, and research opportunities for prospective students. Two arrays: 'phd' and 'master'. Each topic has: id (slug for URL), title, area, summary (1-2 sentences for the card), description (longer paragraph for the detail page), motivation (research problem), objectives (array), methods (array), profile (description of ideal student), outputs (expected outputs), supervisor, co_supervisor (optional), status ('open', 'taken', 'example'). The website automatically renders each topic as a clickable card linking to topic.html?id=<id>. Topics also appear on the supervisor's member.html profile under 'Opportunities & supervised topics'. Edit and commit to update.

phd.title: Endogenous resilience and justice in long-term energy planning
phd.summary: Develop optimization frameworks that endogenously represent resilience to extreme events and distributional justice in capacity-expansion models.
phd.description: This thesis advances integrated decarbonization modeling by embedding resilience and justice metrics directly into long-term capacity-expansion optimization. The work links to the DECARB-R+J project and may include applications to Chilean and Latin-American pathways.
phd.motivation: Long-term energy planning models rarely account for resilience to extreme climate events or for the distributional impacts of policy choices. This thesis closes that gap.
objectives: Formulate endogenous resilience constraints for long-term planning models.
Develop distributional-justice indicators tractable for optimization.
Apply the framework to Chile and benchmark against existing approaches.
phd.profile: Strong background in operations research or applied mathematics; interest in energy and climate policy.
phd.outputs: Three Q1 publications; open-source model release.

phd.title: Power-to-X integration in 100% renewable systems
phd.summary: Quantify the role of Power-to-X technologies as cross-sector flexibility resources in 100%-renewable power systems.
phd.description: Studies the system-level value of Power-to-X (hydrogen, e-fuels, e-chemicals) when used as flexibility for a 100% renewable power system, with attention to economic, technical, and policy dimensions.
phd.motivation: Decarbonizing the energy system requires linking electricity to other sectors. Power-to-X is the bridge — but its system value under different policy regimes is poorly understood.
objectives: Develop high-resolution capacity-expansion models with Power-to-X.
Quantify the system value of P2X under alternative policy regimes.
Extend to multi-country cases in Latin America and Europe.
phd.profile: Quantitative engineering or economics background; programming proficiency.

master.title: Coordinated EV + distributed PV incentives
master.summary: Design and evaluate incentive schemes that coordinate residential adoption of electric vehicles and distributed PV.
master.description: Combines household-level adoption modeling with grid-side analysis to design coordinated incentive packages for EV and PV uptake in Chilean households.
master.motivation: Adoption of electric vehicles and distributed PV is highly correlated, but incentives are typically designed in isolation. Coordinated design unlocks system-level efficiency.
objectives: Design and simulate coordinated incentive schemes.
master.profile: Industrial engineering, economics, or applied math.

master.title: Quantitative indicators of just transition
master.summary: Develop and apply quantitative indicators of procedural and distributional justice in decarbonization.
master.description: Builds a workable set of indicators of just transition for Chilean decarbonization, drawing on the literature and on data from the Chilean electricity sector.
master.motivation: Just-transition concepts are widely discussed but rarely measured. This thesis builds operational indicators that can feed back into policy and modelling.
objectives: Apply them to Chilean transition scenarios.

master.title: Carbon-removal sequestration pathways for Chile
master.summary: Map and assess feasible carbon-removal pathways for Chile under net-zero and net-negative scenarios.
master.description: Surveys candidate carbon-removal technologies and develops scenarios for their deployment in Chile, with attention to land, water, and energy constraints.
master.motivation: Net-zero and net-negative pathways depend on carbon removal at scale. Chile's options are under-studied.
